items.title: Holly Hofmann interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998
items.q: People gave me a lot of Paul Horn and Herbie Mann and you know my parents’ friends gave me a wealth of LPs and things.

ctx.x: And who were the first — of course Frank Wess, any other early jazz flute players effect you?

The flute players not so much. People gave me a lot of Paul Horn and Herbie Mann and you know my parents’ friends gave me a wealth of LPs and things. But they were never playing the flute like I heard the flute. And I mean no disrespect by that, I just heard something different. I heard I guess the flute being a horn. And in those days they were always playing the flute in that, you know, the doublers would play a real burning saxophone solo, and then pick up and only use the flute in a really pretty kind of…
So save the records and give me some clothes or something.
